Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Is Muhammad foretold in the Bible?

The Quran says so plainly and names no chapter. Its claim is given as its own, with what a reader can check.

Part 1 of 3

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ ٱلنَّبِىَّ ٱلْأُمِّىَّ ٱلَّذِى يَجِدُونَهُۥ مَكْتُوبًا عِندَهُمْ فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَٱلْإِنجِيلِ يَأْمُرُهُم بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَىٰهُمْ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَـٰتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْخَبَـٰٓئِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَٱلْأَغْلَـٰلَ ٱلَّتِى كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ ٱلنُّورَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ مَعَهُۥٓ ۙ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written [i.e., described] in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and prohibits them from what is wrong and makes lawful for them what is good and forbids them from what is evil and relieves them of their burden[410] and the shackles which were upon them.[411] So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.

Translator's notes

[410] Difficulties in religious practice. [411] i.e., extreme measures previously required for repentance, and retribution without recourse to compensation.

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:157

The verse says those who follow the Messenger find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. That is a plain statement, made to people who held those two books. Anyone careful of his reputation would avoid such a risk: inviting a people of scripture to open their own book. The verse then gives marks and no chapter number. He commands what is right, forbids what is wrong, allows what is good, lifts people's burdens. Its own measure is what he brought.

A question for you

What would you need in order to judge a claim like this?

If you sayA specific passage.
ThenThe Quran names none, and this app adds none. The third part shows what can be checked instead.
If you sayMarks in the Prophet's own life.
ThenThat is the verse's own measure, and the Gospel has one like it: a tree is known by its fruit.
If you sayThe witness of those who hold those books.
ThenThe Quran calls on that witness, and it has its own Step.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِنِّى رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ إِلَيْكُم مُّصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمُبَشِّرًۢا بِرَسُولٍ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِى ٱسْمُهُۥٓ أَحْمَدُ ۖ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ قَالُوا۟ هَـٰذَا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allāh to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Aḥmad."[1682] But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."[1683]

Translator's notes

[1682] Another name of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ). [1683] i.e., fraud or deception.

Quran · As-Saff 61:6

Translation

“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.

Original · Ancient Greek

Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:17

World English Bible

﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَـٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيْتُكُم مِّن كِتَـٰبٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥ ۚ قَالَ ءَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمْ إِصْرِى ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَقْرَرْنَا ۚ قَالَ فَٱشْهَدُوا۟ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [recall, O People of the Scripture], when Allāh took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], "Whatever I give you of the Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you [must] believe in him and support him." [Allāh] said, "Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My commitment?"[136] They said, "We have acknowledged it." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."

Translator's notes

[136] i.e., Have you accepted this obligation?

Quran · Aal Imran 3:81

The first verse puts this news in the mouth of Jesus: confirming the Torah before him, and bringing good news of a messenger to come after him, whose name is Ahmad. The second gives a wider picture: God took a pledge from the prophets that when a messenger came confirming what they held, they would believe in him and support him. In the Quran's vision no prophet stands alone. Each hands on to the next. This is the Quran's claim, and it is read here as its claim.

A question for you

Which element of this claim seems most important to you?

If you sayThat the prophets form one chain.
ThenThen a Step of its own looks at the one command they all carried.
If you sayThat Jesus spoke of one after him.
ThenThat is what the Quran says. The next part says what can and cannot be checked.
If you sayThat the Quran said this to those who held the books.
ThenThat is where the boldness lies. You may well ask where such confidence comes from.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِنَّهُۥ لَفِى زُبُرِ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ١٩٦ أَوَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُمْ ءَايَةً أَن يَعْلَمَهُۥ عُلَمَـٰٓؤُا۟ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ١٩٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples. And has it not been a sign to them that it is recognized by the scholars of the Children of Israel?

Quran · Ash-Shu'ara 26:196-197

What can honestly be said? The Quran states this, and it names no chapter. This app adds none: it reports the claim as the Quran's, and it does not point to a line and say, this is him. The Quran's own ground is wider: this is in the writings of the ancients, and the learned of Israel knew it. What you can check is the agreement and the marks: one God, the same core commands, what he brought. The verse leaves that with those who know the books.

A question for you

How would you weigh a reading like this?

If you sayOnly a named passage would count.
ThenA strict and fair standard. The Quran gives none, so the marks of the verse may be the place for you to look.
If you sayI look at what he brought.
ThenThat is the first verse's own measure. See what his book and theirs have in common.
If you sayI would ask those who hold those books.
ThenThe Quran itself names that route.

Your reflection

What would you look for in a message that says it comes from God? How would you know it if it came?
